title: They are Coming!
transcript: They want you to think that this position is a win for black because the pawns are completely unstoppable. They're going to run down [music] the board and get a new queen. But don't let them fool you. White has an incredible resource that is going to allow him to win this position. The first move is knight to b6. Now going after this pawn, if it wasn't for the fact that the b2 pawn [music] can be pushed and now if you take here, this is just going to promote. But the key idea of knight to b6 was not to go after this pawn, but to deliver a check on d5. And now after the king moves, the knight can go to c3 and temporarily prevent the promotion. But this is still not as simple as it might seem because if the white knight ever tries to go after this pawn with a fork, black is actually going to be able to draw this game. The c pawn is going to push and the white will have to accept that the only way to stop it is to sacrifice itself. And with a bishop left, white cannot win. But this doesn't mean that there is no way [music] for white to win this position. After knight to b1, the pawn is still stopped and it is going to take much longer for the black king to kick out the knight. And in the meantime, white can put his brilliant plan into motion with king to b6, the only move. The black starts to push the c pawn with the help of the king. But now white can still prevent the promotion for a little bit longer with bishop to d3 [music] defending the c2 square. But after black plays king to b3, it seems like there is no way to stop the pawn. But that's just a lie. Wake up. There is king to b5. And now if the pawn is pushed with the help of the king, both pawns are only one square away from getting a new queen and it seems like they cannot be stopped. But incredibly, out of nowhere, white has created a mating net and bishop to c4 is checkmate. I said too much. I have to go.
